P4 text patterns (if no name or no bio text): for each authorSectionPatterns regex that matches body innerText, find the FIRST element in document order among h2, h3, h4, h5, p, div, section, aside whose textContent matches; container = el.closest("section, article, aside, div") (can be el itself) or parentElement; if container textContent length is 21-2999 chars it becomes authorBioText; name = capture group of nameFromContainer regex on container text. Stops at the first pattern that yields bio text.
P5 CSS fallback (only if no bio text): first element (in authoritySelectors order) whose trimmed textContent is 21-2999 chars becomes authorBioText.

rules.value: hasSocialProfiles is computed (any a[href] whose resolved href contains one of these) but does NOT affect the score.
experiencePatterns (first-person "in my experience", "I've found", "our team", "hands-on", ...) are matched and reported but do NOT affect the score.

scoring.status_mapping: score >= 4 -> pass; score >= 2 -> warning; else fail.

detect.source_procedure: 1. Pick the page templates to evaluate. Static HTML: every *.html (prioritise index.html and article/blog templates). Astro: src/layouts/*.astro plus src/pages/** (and src/content/** frontmatter feeding them). Hugo: layouts/** (baseof.html, partials/head*, single.html), hugo.toml/config.toml params, content/** frontmatter. Eleventy: _includes/**, _layouts/**, src/**, .eleventy.js, _data/**. Next.js app router: app/**/layout.tsx and page.tsx (metadata exports, JSX); pages router: pages/_document.tsx, pages/_app.tsx, <Head> in pages/**. Vite SPA: index.html and src/** components. Evaluate the layout chain that renders a representative content page (blog post/article) and the home page; report per-page if they differ. 2. JSON-LD: collect <script type="application/ld+json"> bodies from templates, plus JSON-LD built in code (Astro set:html={JSON.stringify(obj)}, Next.js <script dangerouslySetInnerHTML> or JSON-LD components, Hugo partials, Eleventy data). Apply parseSchemaForAuthor as described: any Person anywhere (depth <= 5) or an author on Article/BlogPosting/NewsArticle/WebPage/Review/HowTo/Recipe gives a name. If the name is a template variable (e.g. {{ .Params.author }}, {post.data.author}), resolve it from frontmatter/config/site data; if unresolvable, treat as name present but flag. 3. Microdata: grep templates for itemprop="author" and itemtype containing schema.org/Person, and a nested itemprop="name". 4. Meta: grep for <meta name="author">, <meta property="article:author">, <meta name="twitter:creator"> in head templates; Next.js app router: metadata.authors / metadata.twitter.creator in layout/page exports (Next emits meta name="author" from authors); Astro/Hugo/Eleventy SEO components/partials. 5. Trust links: grep all templates (header/footer/nav partials especially) for href values containing "/about", "/contact", "/privacy", "/terms" (substring, raw attribute), and for <address> or itemtype containing PostalAddress. Count distinct kinds; >= 3 earns the point. Also check nav data files (e.g. Hugo menus in config, Astro/Next nav arrays) since links are often data-driven. 6. Authority: +1 if trust scan found any href containing "/about", "/author/", "/contributor/" or "/writer/", or any class containing author-bio / about-author, or itemprop="author" / itemtype containing Person, or a byline/author-box element with 21-2999 chars of text. 7. Expertise: run the 41 expertisePatterns against the concatenation of author bio text, schema Person jobTitle/description/hasCredential/alumniOf/knowsAbout, and the first ~5000 characters of the page visible text (approximate from the template plus the content file markdown, stripping tags). Note that very common words match (see open_questions), so on any page with meaningful English copy this is nearly always true. 8. Sum as in scoring.rules, cap at 5, map status.
detect.llm_criteria: Only the text-pattern name extraction (P4) and the expertise scan depend on rendered visible text. The model should: (a) decide whether visible body copy on a content page contains a byline or author section matching the authorSectionPatterns, and extract "By First Last" style names as the regex would (capitalized 2-4 word sequence after By / Written by / Author:, note the regex has no word boundary so "Nearby Coffee Shop" yields "Coffee Shop"); (b) decide whether the first ~5000 visible characters contain any expertise pattern term (degrees, titles like Founder/Director/Editor/Author/Writer, certifications, Certified/Licensed/Registered, Expert/Specialist/Consultant/Professional, "N years of experience", "Member of", "Featured in", etc.). Mirror the regexes, do not apply a stricter human judgement of genuine expertise.

parity.note: Meta tags, JSON-LD, microdata and trust links in templates are reliably detectable from source. Divergence comes from: JSON-LD or meta injected client side (SPA, tag managers, Yoast-like plugins at runtime); template variables whose values live in CMS/frontmatter; the expertise scan and text-pattern detection run on rendered innerText (first 5000 chars, which includes nav/header text) that source can only approximate; href substring matching runs on raw attribute values after framework rendering (e.g. Next.js <Link href="/about">, Hugo relURL output); navigation built from data files or fetched menus. The extension evaluates a single page; source audits must choose which templates represent it.

checks.fix_summary: Add meta name="author" and a JSON-LD Person (name, jobTitle, sameAs, worksFor) as author of an Article/BlogPosting in the head/layout (Astro layout, Hugo head partial, Next.js metadata.authors plus a JSON-LD script, Eleventy base layout, static index.html), add a visible byline/author bio block (class author-bio) and ensure header/footer link to /about, /contact, /privacy, /terms. Real author name, credentials and bio text must come from the user.

checks.name: Image Alt Text
checks.description: Measures the share of elements with non-empty alt text. Alt text is how AI crawlers and agents understand image content (and is an accessibility baseline), so missing alt leaves images invisible to them.
inputs: rendered DOM: every img element and its alt attribute

scoring.summary: If there are no img elements: pass, 5. Otherwise percentage = round(100 * imagesWithAlt / totalImages), where an image counts only if alt exists and alt.trim() is non-empty. score = round(percentage / 100 * 5).

rules.condition: img counts as having alt iff getAttribute("alt") !== null and alt.trim().length > 0 (alt="" and whitespace-only count as MISSING)

scoring.status_mapping: percentage < 60 -> fail; 60 <= percentage < 90 -> warning; >= 90 -> pass (no images -> pass). Note 50-59% scores 3 but is fail.

detect.source_procedure: Enumerate images that end up as on the evaluated page. Static HTML: every *.html (prioritise index.html and article/blog templates). Astro: src/layouts/*.astro plus src/pages/** (and src/content/** frontmatter feeding them). Hugo: layouts/** (baseof.html, partials/head*, single.html), hugo.toml/config.toml params, content/** frontmatter. Eleventy: _includes/**, _layouts/**, src/**, .eleventy.js, _data/**. Next.js app router: app/**/layout.tsx and page.tsx (metadata exports, JSX); pages router: pages/_document.tsx, pages/_app.tsx, in pages/**. Vite SPA: index.html and src/** components. Count: literal tags in HTML/templates/partials; Astro / from astro:assets (render , alt is required by the component); Next.js from next/image (renders ); Hugo images in layouts and markdown ![alt](src) rendered by Goldmark (markdown image alt becomes alt attribute; empty ![](x) gives alt=""); Eleventy eleventy-img shortcodes; JSX in React/Vue components; markdown/MDX content files for the page. For each, determine alt: literal non-empty string -> has alt; alt="" or missing -> missing; alt bound to an expression (alt={post.title}, alt="{{ .Title }}") -> treat as has alt unless the source value is clearly empty/undefined. Compute percentage and score per rules. Evaluate per page template (home plus a representative content page) and report per page; if a build output exists, parse built HTML instead.

parity.note: Literal templates and built HTML give exact parity. Differences arise from images injected by JavaScript (carousels, lazy loaders, third-party widgets, tracking pixels), CMS content images, components that conditionally render images, and dynamic alt expressions that may evaluate to empty strings. The extension counts every img in the live DOM including tracking pixels and widget images the repo does not contain.

checks.fix_summary: Add descriptive alt attributes to each img in templates, components and markdown (e.g. ![Descriptive text](img.png), <Image alt="...">). The plugin can draft alt text from filename/context but a human should confirm; note that marking decorative images alt="" still counts as missing for this check.

checks.name: Internal Linking
checks.description: Counts same-host links on the page, separating navigation (nav/header/footer) from in-content links, and penalises generic anchor text such as 'click here' in content. Internal links with descriptive anchors help AI crawlers understand site topology and what each linked page is about.
inputs: rendered DOM: all a[href] elements, their href attribute, innerText and ancestor nav/header/footer/[role=navigation]

scoring.summary: Start at 4. Internal = a[href] whose href is not mailto:/tel:/javascript:/# and whose resolved hostname equals the page hostname exactly. 0 internal links -> -3. Else if content links < 3 AND total internal < 5 -> -1. Generic anchor text on content (non-nav) links -> -0.25 each, max -1. finalScore = max(0, round to 1 decimal); status from unfloored value (>= 3 pass, >= 2 warning, else fail); reported score = floor.

rules.condition: href attribute (raw) not starting with 'mailto:', 'tel:', 'javascript:' or '#', and new URL(href, window.location.origin).hostname === window.location.hostname (exact, so www vs apex differ; subdomains are external)
link.closest('nav, header, footer, [role="navigation"]') -> nav link; otherwise content link

text = innerText trimmed lowercased; generic if length < 2 (includes empty, e.g. image-only links) or matches exactly one of: 'click here', 'here', 'read more', 'more', 'link', 'learn more', 'this', 'this link', 'click', 'go', 'see more', 'view', 'details', 'info', '→', '»', '>'
else content links < 3 AND total internal links < 5
descriptivePercentage, uniqueDestinations (distinct pathnames), navToContentRatio: no score effect
finalScore = max(0, round(score*10)/10); reported score = floor(finalScore)

scoring.status_mapping: Based on unfloored finalScore: >= 3 pass, >= 2 warning, else fail. Reported score = Math.floor(finalScore), e.g. 3.75 -> pass/3, 2.5 -> warning/2, 1 (no links) -> fail/1.

detect.source_procedure: Per representative page: 1) Assemble effective HTML: static *.html; Astro layout (src/layouts/*.astro) + page (src/pages/**) + components; Hugo layouts/_default/baseof.html + partials + content Markdown (Markdown links become <a>); Eleventy _includes/** layouts + page content; Next.js app/**/layout.tsx + page.tsx (<Link href> and <a href>), pages router _app/_document + page; Vite SPA components rendering the route. 2) Collect all anchors with href (<a href>, framework <Link href>/<NuxtLink to>, Markdown [text](url)). 3) Classify internal: relative URLs and absolute URLs whose host equals the production host (from site/baseURL in astro.config, hugo.toml baseURL, metadataBase, package homepage, CNAME file); exclude mailto:, tel:, javascript:, '#...'. 4) Mark nav links when inside <nav>, <header>, <footer> or role=navigation (including those in layout partials). 5) Compute visible anchor text (text content excluding alt text) and apply the generic list and length < 2 rule. 6) Apply deductions and thresholds.

parity.note: The extension sees the rendered DOM including JS-injected links (menus, related posts widgets, CMS content) and uses innerText (hidden text excluded, CSS text-transform can apply). Link hrefs built from variables or data files need resolution. Exact hostname comparison depends on the live host (www vs apex, preview domains), so absolute links to the canonical domain can count as external when the audited URL uses a different host.

checks.fix_summary: Add at least 3 in-content internal links (outside nav/header/footer) to related pages with descriptive anchor text, and replace generic anchors ('read more', 'click here', icon-only links) with descriptive text or visually hidden text in the link. The plugin can rewrite generic anchors using the target page title automatically, but choosing which pages to link needs user or model judgment.

checks.name: Accessibility
checks.description: Checks basic semantic structure: a <main> landmark, a <nav> landmark, labelled form inputs, and a minimum count of semantic elements. Semantic landmarks help AI parsers and agents locate the main content and navigation, and are a foundation for accessibility.
inputs: rendered DOM body: semantic elements, ARIA roles/attributes, form inputs and labels, skip links

scoring.summary: Start at 4. Deduct 1.75 if no <main> or [role="main"]; 0.75 if no <nav> or [role="navigation"]; 0.75 if fewer than 50% of visible form inputs are labelled (only when inputs exist); 0.75 if total semantic element count < 5 AND no main. finalScore = max(0, round(score*10)/10); status from finalScore; reported score = floor(finalScore). ARIA counts and skip link are informational only.

rules.condition: semantic element count = number of elements matching each of: main, nav, article, section, aside, header, footer, figure, figcaption (summed)

inputs = 'input:not([type="hidden"]), textarea, select'; an input is labelled if it has an id with a matching label[for=id], or a non-empty aria-label, or a non-empty aria-labelledby, or is inside a <label>. If inputs exist and round(labelled/inputs*100) < 50
finalScore = max(0, round(score*10)/10); reported score = Math.floor(finalScore)

scoring.status_mapping: Using decimal finalScore: >= 3 pass, >= 2 warning, else fail. Reported points = floor. Reachable outcomes: 4 pass (no issues); 3.25 pass/3 (missing nav or poor labels); 2.5 warning/2 (nav + labels missing); 2.25 warning/2 (missing main only, >= 5 semantic elements); 1.5 fail/1 (missing main, <5 semantic, or main+nav); 0.75 fail/0; 0 fail/0.

detect.source_procedure: Evaluate the full page markup that composes each route: layout + page + components. Static HTML: each *.html. Astro: src/layouts/*.astro plus src/pages/** and imported src/components/**. Hugo: layouts/_default/baseof.html, single.html, list.html, partials/**. Eleventy: _includes/** layouts plus page templates. Next.js: app/**/layout.tsx + page.tsx and components (JSX tags <main>, <nav>, role="main"); pages router: _app/_document + pages/**. Vite SPA: index.html is usually just <div id="app">, so inspect root components (src/App.vue|tsx, router views). Count tags and role attributes, check form inputs for labels, then apply the deductions.

parity.note: The extension counts elements in the live DOM after JavaScript, including third-party widgets (cookie banners, chat widgets with unlabeled inputs) that are not in the repo. Component frameworks may render <main>/<nav> from library components whose names do not reveal the tag. Conditionally rendered elements may be present or absent at runtime.

checks.fix_summary: Wrap the primary content in <main> and site navigation in <nav> in the base layout (Astro layout, Hugo baseof.html, Eleventy base layout, Next.js root layout.tsx, Vite App component); add <label for> or aria-label to form inputs. Adding main alone removes the largest deduction.

checks.name: Server-Rendered Content
checks.description: Compares the raw HTML the server returns (no JavaScript) with the rendered DOM to see how much of the visible text, the H1 and the title exist before hydration. Most AI crawlers and agents do not execute JavaScript, so client-only content is invisible to them.
inputs: raw HTML of the page via plain GET (status, content-type, body, redirected, truncated)
rendered DOM: document.body text, first <h1>, document.title

scoring.summary: Fetch raw HTML. Unreachable or non-200 -> warning 3 (inconclusive). Non-HTML content-type -> pass 6. Otherwise parse raw HTML, count words in raw body and rendered body (removing script, style, noscript, template, svg). ratio = raw/dom capped at 1 (1 if dom < 30 words). Start 6: empty SPA root in raw HTML -> 0; else ratio < 0.25 -> 0; else ratio < 0.6 -> 3. Then -1 if rendered H1 is missing from raw HTML, -1 if rendered title missing from raw HTML, floor at 0. Status >= 5 pass, >= 3 warning, else fail; a fail on a redirected or truncated fetch is raised to warning 3.

rules.condition: isUnreachable(page): status 0, 403, 429, 503 or timedOut (fetch timeout 3000 ms)
Content-Type present and does not match /text\/html|application\/xhtml/i
rules.note: missing Content-Type is treated as HTML

rules.condition: clone body, remove 'script, style, noscript, template, svg', textContent, trim, split /\s+/. rawWordCount from DOMParser-parsed raw HTML body; domWordCount from live document.body.
ratio = 1 if domWordCount < 30, else min(1, rawWordCount / domWordCount)
first selector in order ['#root', '#app', '#__next', '#__nuxt', '#___gatsby', '#svelte', '#q-app', '[data-reactroot]'] whose FIRST matching element in raw HTML has textContent.trim() === ''
rendered DOM has an <h1> with non-empty text AND raw HTML has no <h1> element at all
document.title non-empty AND raw HTML <title> empty or missing
status fail AND (page.redirected OR page.truncated (body > 2 MB default cap))

scoring.status_mapping: score >= 5 pass, 3-4 warning, 0-2 fail; fail downgraded to warning with score 3 when the raw fetch was redirected or truncated; unreachable and non-200 are warning 3.
scoring.inconclusive: Unreachable (0/403/429/503/timeout) or any non-200 status returns warning with score 3 of 6 and details.inconclusive true; never a fail.

detect.source_procedure: 1) Identify rendering mode per stack. Static HTML: raw == rendered unless scripts inject content; inspect body. Astro: default static/SSR output is server-rendered; flag components with client:only (render nothing server-side) and pages whose main content is in a client:only island. Hugo/Eleventy: static output, server-rendered unless a JS framework mounts into an empty div. Next.js: app router server components render HTML; flag pages that are 'use client' with data fetched in useEffect, dynamic(() => ..., { ssr: false }) around main content, or output: 'export' pages with empty shells; pages router: getServerSideProps/getStaticProps render HTML, pure client fetching does not. Vite SPA (React/Vue/Svelte without SSR): index.html has an empty <div id="root"> or <div id="app"> -> score 0. 2) Where a build is possible, build and inspect the output HTML (dist/, out/, public/ for Hugo, _site/ for Eleventy, .next/server/app/*.html) and compute rawWordCount from it. 3) Check the output HTML for the app-root selectors with empty text, for an <h1> element and non-empty <title>. 4) Estimate rendered word count from the source components/content; if raw >= 60% of it, full credit. 5) Apply penalties and thresholds exactly.
detect.llm_criteria: Decide whether the page's main text, H1 and <title> are emitted in server HTML or only after client JavaScript runs. Estimate the share of final visible words present in server HTML and bucket it: < 25% -> 0, 25-59% -> 3, >= 60% -> 6. Any SPA mount node from the selector list that is empty in server HTML is an automatic 0 (even if other content exists).

parity.note: The extension diffs a live fetch against the live DOM; from source, the rendered DOM must be estimated. Middleware, edge rendering, A/B scripts, CMS content, consent walls, bot-specific responses and host behavior (redirects, 404/401 pages, compression) are invisible to source analysis. Building the site gives near-exact raw HTML for static generators, but the rendered word count still needs estimation when client JS adds content.

checks.fix_summary: Serve meaningful HTML without JavaScript: use SSR/SSG or prerendering (Astro default output instead of client:only, Next.js server components or getStaticProps instead of useEffect fetching or ssr:false, vite-plugin-ssr/prerender or a static generator for Vite SPAs), and make sure <h1> and <title> are in the server HTML (Next metadata export, Astro/Hugo layouts). These are architectural changes the plugin can outline or partially apply but the user must approve.

checks.name: Markdown for Agents
checks.description: Checks whether the page offers a Markdown representation to AI agents: via HTTP content negotiation (Accept: text/markdown), an advertised alternate (<link rel=alternate type=text/markdown> or Link header), or an undiscoverable .md sibling file. Markdown gives agents the same content at a fraction of the tokens of HTML.
inputs: HTTP GET of page with 'Accept: text/markdown, text/html;q=0.9' (status, Content-Type, Link, Vary, X-Markdown-Tokens headers)
HTTP GET of .md probe URL (1500 ms timeout)

scoring.summary: Tiered, first match wins: (0) negotiated request unreachable => warning 3 inconclusive; (1) negotiated response ok AND Content-Type matches /text\/markdown/i => pass 5; (2) Link header advertises markdown alternate OR DOM has a markdown alternate <link> => warning 3; (3) .md probe returns non-HTML markdown => warning 2; (4) otherwise fail 0. Vary: Accept and X-Markdown-Tokens are recorded but not scored.

rules.condition: probe URL: strip query and hash; path '' or '/' => '/index.md'; last path segment contains '.' => no probe (null); else pathname with trailing '/' removed + '.md'
isUnreachable(negotiation): status in [0, 403, 429, 503] or timedOut (3000 ms page timeout)

Link response header matches /text\/markdown/i AND /rel="?alternate"?/i (tested independently on the whole header string) OR document.querySelector('link[rel~="alternate"][type="text/markdown"], link[rel~="alternate"][type="text/x-markdown"]') exists
probe response ok AND NOT HTML (Content-Type not /text\/html|application\/xhtml/i and body not /^\s*<(!doctype|html)/i) AND (Content-Type matches /markdown/i OR body matches /^\s*#\s+\S/)

scoring.status_mapping: Fixed per tier: 5 pass, 3 warning, 2 warning, 0 fail.
scoring.inconclusive: If the Accept: text/markdown request is unreachable (status 0/403/429/503 or timed out), returns warning with 3 points and details.inconclusive = true, regardless of DOM alternate or probe results.

detect.source_procedure: Tier 1 (negotiation) is server behaviour: look for evidence in host/server config - Cloudflare 'Markdown for Agents' is a zone setting (not in repo); check functions/_middleware.(js|ts) (Cloudflare Pages), middleware.ts (Next.js/Vercel), netlify/edge-functions/**, vercel.json 'rewrites'/'has' on header accept, nginx/Caddy configs, or server code that branches on Accept: text/markdown and sets Content-Type: text/markdown. If found, assume pass (unverified). Tier 2: grep page templates/head for <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" (static HTML *.html; Astro src/layouts/*.astro; Hugo layouts/_default/baseof.html, layouts/partials/head*.html, or outputFormats markdown in hugo.toml with alternate output; Eleventy _includes/**; Next.js app router metadata.alternates.types['text/markdown'] in app/**/layout.tsx|page.tsx, pages router <Head> in _document/_app; Vite index.html), and for Link headers containing text/markdown and rel=alternate in _headers (Netlify/Cloudflare Pages), netlify.toml [[headers]], vercel.json headers. Tier 3: check whether a .md file will be served at <path>.md or /index.md (public/**/*.md, static/**/*.md, Hugo markdown output format, build output) that starts with '# Heading' or will get a markdown Content-Type.
detect.llm_criteria: Judge whether any server/edge code or host config found actually returns Content-Type text/markdown when the request Accept header contains text/markdown for the audited page (not just for a single API route). If unsure, do not award tier 1; fall back to tiers 2/3.

parity.note: Content negotiation is a runtime server/CDN property (often a Cloudflare dashboard toggle) and usually invisible in the repo, so source can under-report tier 1. DOM alternate links injected by JavaScript are seen by the extension but not in static templates. The .md probe depends on the host serving .md files with a non-HTML content type and on SPA fallbacks not returning index.html. Unreachable/WAF cases (inconclusive 3) cannot be reproduced from source.

checks.fix_summary: Auto-add <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="/page.md"> to the head template (or Next.js metadata.alternates.types) and a Link header via _headers / netlify.toml / vercel.json, plus generate .md copies of pages at build time; this reaches 3/5. Full 5/5 needs server or edge content negotiation (Cloudflare Markdown for Agents toggle, a Pages/_middleware or Next.js middleware that returns text/markdown for Accept: text/markdown), which the user must enable or approve.

checks.name: Agent-Usable Controls
checks.description: Checks that interactive controls are operable through the accessibility tree, which is how browsing agents act on a page: buttons have accessible names and are focusable, links have real hrefs, click handlers are not on bare divs/spans, and personal-data inputs declare autocomplete. An icon-only button or an href-less link is invisible as an action to an agent.
inputs: rendered DOM: all <a> elements and their href/aria/name/id/onclick attributes
rendered DOM: div/span/li/p/img/td elements with an inline onclick attribute
rendered DOM: all <input> elements with type, name, id, autocomplete
hidden / aria-hidden="true" attributes on elements and ancestors

scoring.summary: Four categories, 1 point each. Elements inside (or being) [hidden] or [aria-hidden="true"] are ignored. For each category: if it has 0 elements it earns 1 point; otherwise it earns 1 point when Math.round((total - problems) / total * 100) >= 90. If all four categories are empty the check passes with 4 and a 'no interactive controls' message.

rules.condition: buttons: elements = 'button, [role="button"], input[type="submit"], input[type="button"], input[type="reset"], input[type="image"]' not hidden. Problem (max one per element) if no accessible name, OR role="button" on a non-native element (native = button, input, select, textarea, summary, a[href]) without a tabindex attribute
rules.points: +1 if pass rate >= 90% or no buttons

rules.condition: accessible name order: non-blank aria-label; text of elements referenced by aria-labelledby ids; trimmed textContent (includes visually hidden text); title; value attribute; alt attribute; descendant img[alt] with non-blank alt; descendant 'svg > title' text; input type submit/reset with nothing else still counts as named

links: all <a> except role="button" and hidden ones. Problem if href is missing, blank, exactly '#', or starts with 'javascript:' (case-insensitive, trimmed), UNLESS the anchor has aria-haspopup or aria-expanded, OR it is a named anchor (has name or id, has no text content, and has no onclick)
rules.points: +1 if pass rate >= 90% or no links

rules.condition: fakeClickables: 'div[onclick], span[onclick], li[onclick], p[onclick], img[onclick], td[onclick]' that have no role attribute at all and are not hidden. Problem if no tabindex attribute
rules.note: Only literal inline onclick attributes; listeners attached with addEventListener or framework handlers (React onClick, Vue @click, Svelte on:click, Alpine @click) are not visible and never count

rules.condition: autocomplete: <input> elements not hidden. Candidate if type (lowercased, default 'text') is not in ['hidden','password','search','checkbox','radio','submit','button','reset','file','image','range','color'] AND (type is 'email' or 'tel' OR `${name} ${id}` matches /(^|[-_ ])(f(irst)?name|l(ast)?name|fullname|surname|address|street|city|zip|postal|postcode|phone|tel|email|country|state|company|organization)/i). Problem if autocomplete attribute is missing, blank, or 'off'
rules.points: +1 if pass rate >= 90% or no candidates

scoring.status_mapping: score 4 pass, 2-3 warning, 0-1 fail.

detect.source_procedure: Prefer scanning built HTML output (dist/, _site/, public/ after hugo, out/ or .next prerendered HTML) with an HTML parser and applying the rules exactly. Without a build, scan markup sources: static *.html; Astro src/**/*.astro (template part after frontmatter); Hugo layouts/**/*.html and shortcodes; Eleventy _includes/** and src/** templates (njk, liquid, md with HTML); Next.js/React app/**, pages/**, components/**/*.tsx|jsx (map JSX: className ignored, aria-label/aria-labelledby/title/alt/tabIndex=tabindex/autoComplete=autocomplete, href; React onClick does NOT render an onclick attribute so do not count it as a fake clickable); Vite SPA index.html plus src/** components. For each file collect buttons, anchors, inline onclick elements, and inputs; skip elements inside hidden or aria-hidden="true" wrappers; compute per-category pass rate per page (or per component when pages cannot be composed) and apply the >= 90% threshold. When labels come from expressions ({t('save')}, {{ .Title }}), treat as named if the expression yields text.

parity.note: The extension sees the live DOM, including controls rendered by client JS, third-party widgets (chat bubbles, cookie banners, embeds) and CMS content, all of which are absent from source. Per-page percentages depend on how components compose into a page, so component-level source scans can differ from the per-URL result. CSS-hidden elements are counted by both (only hidden/aria-hidden are excluded).

checks.fix_summary: Add autocomplete tokens (email, tel, given-name, family-name, street-address, postal-code, country-name, organization) to personal-data inputs; give icon-only buttons aria-label or visually hidden text; replace href-less or '#'/javascript: anchors with <button> or real hrefs; replace div/span onclick with <button> or add role/tabindex. Autocomplete and tabindex are auto-fixable in templates; label wording and link targets need user confirmation.

checks.name: Agent Protocol Discovery
checks.description: Checks whether the site publishes machine-readable discovery artifacts (MCP server card, A2A agent card, agent skills index, RFC 9727 API catalog, OpenAPI, OAuth metadata, /.well-known/ai) or declarative WebMCP tool annotations, so AI agents can find and use its tools and APIs without reading docs. Conditional: returns 'na' (removed from the score denominator) when the site shows no API or agent surface.
inputs: HTTP GET of 11 well-known / discovery paths on the page origin (body, status, content-type)
rendered DOM: a[href] (first 500), link[rel~=service-desc|describedby], script[type=application/ld+json], elements with [toolname] or [tooldescription]

scoring.summary: Probes 11 paths (concurrency 6, 1500 ms timeout each). A probe counts as found only if response.ok, the body is not HTML, and the path's validator passes on the parsed JSON. Found artifacts are grouped into categories (mcp, a2a, skills, api, oauth, ai) and WebMCP annotations add a 'webmcp' category. Score is by number of distinct categories: 3+ -> 6 pass, 2 -> 5 pass, 1 -> 3 warning. If none found: if every probe was unreachable -> na (inconclusive); else if the page shows same-site API evidence -> fail 0; else -> na (not applicable, excluded from denominator).

rules.condition: GET each path on origin with backgroundFetch(method GET, timeoutMs 1500), bounded concurrency 6. Order of ARTIFACTS list below.

contentType = Content-Type header (case-insensitive). isHtml = /text\/html|application\/xhtml/i on content-type OR body matches /^\s*<(!doctype|html)/i. If body non-empty and not HTML, JSON.parse(body); json = null on parse failure.
artifact found only when probe.ok (2xx) AND NOT isHtml AND validator(json, probe) returns true (exceptions -> false)

rules.label: A2A agent card
rules.validator: json is a non-array object with truthy 'name'

rules.label: Agent card
rules.validator: json is a non-array object with truthy 'name'

rules.label: Agent skills index
rules.validator: json is an object or an array

rules.label: API catalog (RFC 9727)
rules.validator: json is an object with truthy 'linkset' OR content-type matches /linkset/i

rules.label: AI metadata
rules.validator: not HTML and body.trim() non-empty (any text format, JSON not required)

rules.condition: 0 categories AND every probe isUnreachable (status 0, 403, 429, 503, or timedOut)
rules.note: details.inconclusive = true; checked BEFORE API evidence

rules.condition: 0 categories AND at least one probe reached AND findApiEvidence() non-empty
0 categories AND at least one probe reached AND no API evidence

Scan first 500 a[href]; resolve against page URL; keep only same-site links (lowercase, strip leading 'www.' from both hosts; equal, or one endsWith '.'+other). Evidence if first path segment (lowercased) is one of [api, apis, developer, developers, docs, documentation, graphql, swagger, openapi, api-docs, api-reference] OR link hostname matches /^(api|apis|developers?|docs)\./i. Collect up to 5 unique origin+pathname samples.
Also evidence: any link[rel~="service-desc"] or link[rel~="describedby"]; any script[type="application/ld+json"] whose text matches /"@type"\s*:\s*"WebAPI"/i

scoring.status_mapping: Explicit per branch: 1 category -> warning (3); 2 -> pass (5); 3+ -> pass (6); none found + API evidence -> fail (0); none found + no evidence or all probes unreachable -> na with applicable:false (maxScore 6 removed from the 138 denominator by ScoringEngine).
scoring.inconclusive: If no artifact is found and ALL 11 probes are unreachable (status 0/403/429/503 or timed out), returns status 'na', applicable false, details.inconclusive true, score 0 - so it is excluded from the denominator rather than half credit. If at least one probe was reached, unreachable individual probes are simply treated as not found.

detect.source_procedure: 1) Locate the static/public root per stack: static HTML: repo root or build dir; Astro: public/; Hugo: static/; Eleventy: passthrough-copied dirs from .eleventy.js (addPassthroughCopy) or src/; Next.js: public/ plus app/.well-known/**/route.ts or pages/api; Vite SPA: public/. 2) For each of the 11 paths, check whether a file exists at <publicRoot><path> (also route handlers producing it, e.g. Next app/.well-known/api-catalog/route.ts, Astro src/pages/.well-known/*.json.ts, Hugo content/layouts outputs). 3) Parse the file and apply the exact validator (object, name, linkset, openapi/swagger, issuer, resource; /.well-known/ai any non-empty non-HTML text). For /.well-known/api-catalog (no extension) also check host config (_headers, netlify.toml, vercel.json headers) for Content-Type containing 'linkset' as an alternate pass. 4) Check host rewrite config (_redirects, vercel.json rewrites, netlify.toml) for SPA catch-all rewrites that would serve index.html for missing paths (those are HTML and never count). 5) Grep templates/layouts/components for attributes toolname= or tooldescription= (WebMCP). 6) Count distinct categories and score. 7) If zero: scan templates for same-site links whose first path segment is in the API list or whose host is api./apis./developer(s)./docs. subdomain of the site domain, for <link rel=service-desc|describedby>, and JSON-LD with @type WebAPI; also consider presence of an actual API in the repo (pages/api, app/api, openapi.yaml). Evidence -> fail 0; none -> na.
detect.llm_criteria: Judge only for the no-artifact case: does the site have a developer or API surface? Mirror the extension: same-site links to /api, /apis, /developer(s), /docs, /documentation, /graphql, /swagger, /openapi, /api-docs, /api-reference (first segment only) or to api./apis./developer(s)./docs. subdomains; a service-desc/describedby link; a WebAPI JSON-LD entity. Links to third-party APIs or anchor text alone do NOT count. The extension only inspects the analyzed page's links, so for parity evaluate the site's main layout/nav/footer plus the target page.

parity.note: Artifacts can be served dynamically (edge functions, reverse proxies to an API host, framework route handlers) or set by the host, and Content-Type (relevant for api-catalog linkset and HTML detection) is decided by the server. API evidence in the extension is evaluated on the single rendered page, so links injected by JS or present only on other pages differ. WebMCP attributes added at runtime by JS are visible to the extension (rendered DOM) but may not be in source. The 'all probes unreachable' na branch cannot be reproduced from source.

checks.fix_summary: Publish discovery JSON under the public root (public/.well-known/ for Astro/Next/Vite, static/.well-known/ for Hugo, passthrough for Eleventy): e.g. /.well-known/api-catalog linkset (served with Content-Type application/linkset+json via _headers, netlify.toml or vercel.json headers), /.well-known/openapi.json, an MCP server card at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, and OAuth metadata if auth is used. Content (endpoints, auth servers, tool list) must come from the user, so the plugin drafts skeletons only; for content-only sites, no fix is needed (na).
